summary.short: Amends Business and Professions Code Chapter 22757: from 1 January 2027, large online platforms must detect and display provenance data and GenAI hosting platforms may not offer systems lacking disclosures; from 1 January 2028, capture device makers must offer and default latent disclosures; $5,000 civil penalty per violation.
summary.long: Amends Business and Professions Code chapter 22757 (sections 22757.1 to 22757.4) and adds sections 22757.3.1 to 22757.3.3. Large online platforms (public-facing social media, file-sharing, mass messaging or stand-alone search engines exceeding 2,000,000 unique monthly users) must, from 1 January 2027, detect standards-compliant provenance data, provide a user interface disclosing system provenance data, let users inspect it, and not knowingly strip it or digital signatures. GenAI hosting platforms may not knowingly make available a GenAI system that lacks disclosures under Section 22757.3, a section not reproduced in this document. From 1 January 2028, capture device manufacturers must offer users an option to embed latent disclosures (manufacturer name, device name and version, time and date) and embed them by default, where technically feasible and standards-compliant. Violators are liable for a $5,000 civil penalty per violation, with each day a discrete violation, in actions by the Attorney General, a city attorney or a county counsel, plus prevailing-plaintiff fees; injunctive relief applies to violations by third-party licensees under Section 22757.3(c)(3). The chapter is operative 2 August 2026 (Section 6). Covered providers are generative AI creators with over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users publicly accessible in California.

No bill number or enabling act is stated. Operative dates differ by section: §§22757.3.1 and 22757.3.2 from January 1, 2027; §22757.3.3 from January 1, 2028; §22757.6 states the chapter is operative August 2, 2026. §22757.3.2(a) and §22757.4(c) refer to §22757.3, which is outside this text. evidence.quote: distribute content to more than 100 users simultaneously
“Artificial intelligence” or “AI” means an engineered or machine-based system that varies in its level of autonomy
“Capture device” means a device that can record photographs, audio, or video content
“Capture device manufacturer” means a person who produces a capture device for sale in the state
“Covered provider” means a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system
“Digital signature” means a cryptography-based method that identifies the user or entity that attests to the information provided
“Generative artificial intelligence system” or “GenAI system” means an artificial intelligence that can generate derived synthetic content
“GenAI hosting platform” means an internet website or application that makes available for download the source code or model weights
“Large online platform” means a public-facing social media platform, file-sharing platform, mass messaging platform, or stand-alone search engine
“Latent” means present but not manifest.
“Manifest” means easily perceived, understood, or recognized by a natural person.
“Mass messaging platform” means a direct messaging platform that allows users to distribute content to more than 100 users simultaneously.
“Metadata” means structural or descriptive information about data.

definitions.defined_in: Civil Code § 1798.140 (by reference, Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.1(m))

evidence.quote: “Personal information” has the same meaning as defined in Section 1798.140 of the Civil Code.
“Personal provenance data” means provenance data that contains either of the following
“Provenance data” means data that is embedded into digital content, or that is included in the digital content’s metadata
“System provenance data” means provenance data that is not reasonably capable of being associated with a particular user

obligations.summary: A large online platform must detect compliant provenance data embedded in or attached to content, provide a user interface disclosing the availability of system provenance data and related authenticity information, and let users inspect that data by the listed means.

evidence.provision: Business and Professions Code § 22757.3.1(a)(2)(A), with (a)(1), (a)(3) and (c)
evidence.quote: Provide a user interface to disclose the availability of system provenance data that reliably indicates that the content was generated or substantially altered by a GenAI system or captured by a capture device.

obligations.summary: A large online platform shall not knowingly strip system provenance data or digital signatures that comply with widely adopted specifications from content uploaded or distributed on the platform, to the extent technically feasible.

evidence.quote: A large online platform shall not, to the extent technically feasible, knowingly strip any system provenance data or digital signature

obligations.summary: A GenAI system hosting platform shall not knowingly make available a GenAI system that does not place the disclosures required under Section 22757.3.

evidence.quote: A GenAI system hosting platform shall not knowingly make available a GenAI system that does not place disclosures pursuant to Section 22757.3.

obligations.summary: A capture device manufacturer must give users the option to include latent disclosures (manufacturer name, device name and version, time and date) in captured content, and must embed latent disclosures by default, for devices first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028.
obligations.applies_from: For capture devices first produced for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028
obligations.conditional_on: Only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body (§ 22757.3.3(b))

evidence.quote: Provide a user with the option to include a latent disclosure in content captured by the capture device
